newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs higher due to investor demand for cash bonds.
newsitem.headline: JGBs higher due to investor demand for cash bonds.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was slightly higher by midday on Wednesday, boosted by strong investor demand for cash bonds, traders said.
Investors, such as investment trusts and city banks, were detected buying the 194th 10-year JGBs, a manager at a city bank's securities unit said.
Talk in the early morning of large-lot buying of the 182nd 10-year JGBs also boosted the market, a trust bank trader said.
The June stood at 127.03 by midday, up slightly from the previous day's close of 126.98.
The lack of an outright bond-uying operation by the Bank of Japan this morning had little impact on the market, traders said.

"There is talk that the BOJ may conduct an outright bond-buying operation on the 24th (Thursday)," the first trader said. The trader said he felt most market players are not expecting the BOJ to reduce the amount of its monthly outright purchases of JGBs.
There will be little impact even if the BOJ does reduce its outright bond buying, some traders said.

"I personally think the BOJ will cut its outright JGB purchases. But I do not think JGBs will fall on account of this, unless investors stop their frenzied buying of cash JGBs," a trader for another city bank's securities unit said.

"Even if the BOJ reduces its outright bond buying, that will only mean a reduction (in JGB buying) of 100 billion yen per month or about one trillion yen annually. I think investors will be more than happy to fill that vacuum," he said.
The BOJ has conducted two outright bond buying operations per month and bought 100 billion yen worth of JGBs each time since January.
Its last outright bond-buying operation was on April 11, when it bought 100 billion yen worth of JGBs.
The central bank most recently reduced the amount of its monthly outright JGB purchases to 200 billion yen from 400 billion yen in December.
The BOJ said the reduction was due to an easing of an year-end fund shortage and a slowdown in bank note growth.
Traders said a forthcoming launch of straight bonds by Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc is unlikely to have a negative impact on JGBs.
Tokyo Electric Power is likely to launch about 100 billion yen worth of 10-year straight bonds on Thursday, a senior trader for another city bank's securities unit said.
A news conference by BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita due at 3 p.m. (0600 GMT) is unlikely to provide fresh trading incentives, traders said.
Traders said the rescue of all 24 Japanese among the hostages freed from the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima had not had much direct effect on JGBs.
